Early, unsigned build of Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI.

## What's new since 0.3.0

- **Debug logs.** Settings, General, Troubleshooting has a new **Save debug logs** switch, off by default. While it is on, each launch writes a log to `Logs/` in your working folder: what the app did, step by step, and the reason and stack of a crash. The newest 10 logs are kept. Logs never contain your Hugging Face token or your audio. See Troubleshooting in the README.
- **A transcription keeps going when you open another file.** Before, opening another audio file cancelled the run and cleared its result. Now the run goes on in the background and its sidebar row says **Transcribing…**. Opening the file again brings back its progress or its result. One file is transcribed at a time.
- **Hugging Face token.** **Save and check** shows that it is checking. It says plainly when Hugging Face rejects a token, and doesn't keep that token. When the token is accepted, it shows the account. The sheet also says that the three statements have to be ticked before the download can start.
- **Layout.** The inspector is open by default and remembers your choice; its button is the last toolbar item. The playback position no longer runs into the Transcribe button. The MIDI file you drag into Finder or a DAW now sits in an Export section of the inspector, with its name. Threads is on the right, like the other settings. The narrowest window is 1104 pt wide, so both toolbars fit with the inspector open.
- **Fixes.**
  - Cancelling the first-use download alert no longer leaves a stuck "Downloading…" panel.
  - A licence sheet that closes without an answer no longer leaves the download waiting for good.
  - Dropping a MIDI file, or something that isn't audio, on the window tells you what to do instead of copying it into `Audio/`.
  - When you open a file while another is still loading, the one you opened last is shown.
  - In rare cases, stopping a run whose engine had already exited could close the app without a crash report. It can't any more.

## Models and licences

| Model | Licence | Download |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MuScriptor small, medium, large | CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial use only | 0.2 to 2.7 GB, gated on Hugging Face |
| Piano (ONNX) | CC BY 4.0, credit required | 154 MB |
| Basic Pitch | Apache-2.0 | built in |

MuScriptor needs a Hugging Face account, accepted terms and a read token in Settings. The app code is Apache-2.0; third-party licences are in the About window and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Known limits

- Apple silicon only, not notarized.
- A crash when dropping audio on a window that already shows a file was reported but couldn't be reproduced. The drop path was hardened. If it happens again, please turn on debug logs and send the log together with the `.ips` report from `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports`.
- The editor uses a fixed 120 bpm, 4/4 grid and notes between C1 and B6; saving writes notes, velocities and track instruments only.
- The piano model handles one instrument. No OGG decoding.
- The maintainer's Mac is Intel and cannot run this build, so the arm64 app itself has not been run by hand. The changes were checked in a Debug build on Intel. Please report anything that looks wrong.
